newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says fiscal debt flat without one-off items.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says fiscal debt flat without one-off items.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank Monday said that if extraordinary one-off debt issues were excluded from official figures, its debt stock would have remained almost constant over the past year.

The head of the bank's economics department, Altamir Lopes, said that if items such as the 8.0 billion real Banco do Brasil recapitalization deal had been excluded, the "net fiscal debt" in September would stand at 241.78 billion reais.
That represented 31.9 percent of gross domestic product compared with a net fiscal debt of 208.44 billion reais or 29.9 percent of GDP in December 1995, Lopes said.

In addition to Banco do Brasil, the bank listed court orders withdrawing money from the monetary reserve fund, privatization receipts, renegotiated debt and interest payments, and exchange rate variations on external debt as one-off items.
In total, the items, which Lopes called the "skeletons" of 1996, amounted to 14.4 billion reais.
Lopes said these skeletons had an impact on debt, but not on the fiscal accounts.
"We've always made this calculation, but decided to present it today so analysts can use it," he said.
